newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK civil servants join in anti-Japanese protest.
newsitem.headline: HK civil servants join in anti-Japanese protest.

text.p: Hong Kong civil servants and students braved heavy rain and took to the street on Saturday to protest against Japan's claim to a group of disputed islands in East China Sea.

The demonstrations were the latest in a growing wave of anti-Japanese protests in Hong Kong sparked by Japan's sovereignty claim over the islands, known as the Diaoyus in Chinese and Senkakus in Japanese.

More than 40 government employees and 20 students planned to hand a petition to the Japanese Consulate in the territory's central business district, demanding the Japanese government to abandon its claim of the islands.
But the mission was closed and protesters plastered their petition letters on the door of the consulate instead.
The students also tore up a paper replica of the Japanese flag to vent their outrage.

China issued a stinging attack on Japan on Saturday, accusing Tokyo of conniving with rightwingers who have built a lighthouse on a group of disputed East China Sea islands and describing ties as distressed.

"It is incomprehensible that the Japanese government has taken no effective measures to prohibit such activities," said a commentary carried in the Communist Party mouthpiece, the People's Daily said.
"Instead, it has taken a laissez-faire attitude and even connived at these activities, which have damaged Sino-Japanese friendship," it said.
A simmering dispute over the islands, flared in July after a rightist Japanese group built a lighthouse on one of the uninhabited but potentially resource-rich islands.
The uninhabited archipelago lies 300 km (190 miles) west of the Japanese island of Okinawa and 200 km (125 miles) northeast of Taiwan. They are claimed by Beijing, Taipei and Tokyo.
